title: Hilmi Pasha telegrams, palace to Yemen 1896-1902 (Koc University HPBK): systems A and B

plaintext.source: none found; the black-ink words over some groups are the receiving clerk's partial reading

transcription.source: HPBK 600 at 2054 px, first two lines only
transcription.notes: 6 of about 45 groups on one of 12 sheets; digits approximate.

plaintext.source: none found; dark letters and words over some numerals are the receiving clerk's partial reading

transcription.notes: Pale pencil numerals; no transcription made.

system.summary: Two numeric systems of Yemen telegrams: A five-digit groups with clear words and clerk glosses; B two- and three-digit numerals with clerk letters over them; both unverified.
system.notes: System B seems to mix two-digit single-letter numerals with three-digit word or suffix numerals (668 = -nde on 599 twice); not tested.

prior_solution.where: Not on DECODE as far as known.py shows; Ben-Bassat (Turcica 46, 2015) treats Ottoman WWI ciphers, not these.

conditions.human_role: Task given by the project; no target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Image route corrected: IIIF page id equals the item id (pixel comparison of 587); 2000-px pages fetched for 587, 602, 576, 578, 599, 600, 725.
Hand reading of the top of 599 and 578 (B) and two lines of 600 (A).

B mixes two-digit letter numerals with three-digit word numerals: numeral 668 has the suffix -nde written over it twice on 599; A groups are not B regrouped (a six-letter word over a five-digit group).
Colour separation of the pale pencil from the dark ink by grey threshold.

outcome.method_basis: No numeral table could be built: the pencil numerals were not transcribable by hand reading in this session.
outcome.notes: Open: transcription of B (599, 578) against clear same-day sheets 725/748; A glosses.
